children: Our Bureau Kolkata: India's largest gold-loan company Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit for the second quarter at 3,278 crore, backed by 42% expansion in business while asset quality deteriorated.

The net profit was 2,412 crore in the year-ago period. On a standalone basis, the company's second-quarter net profit stood at 2,977 crore, up 27% over 2,345 crore in the year-ago quarter. Muthoot's consolidated assets under management (AUM) grew 42% year-on-year to 2.09 lakh crore at the end of September.

Out of this, the gold loan portfolio stood at 1.93 lakh crore. Its standalone AUM grew at the same pace to 1.88 lakh crore, of which gold loan was 1.79 lakh crore. The company's standalone gross non-performing assets ratio jumped to 3.87% at the end of September from 2.28% three months prior. Muthoot's subsidiary Belstar Microfinance earned a 78 crore net profit for the quarter under review, widening from 66 crore in the first quarter. Its asset quality improved with gross NPA ratio falling to 3.26% from 4.58% a year back. Its first-half net profit stood at 144 crore compared to a loss of 160 crore in the year-ago six-month period.

title: Gold Loan Boom Lifts Muthoot's Q2 Profit by 36%
